item.title: Congreso de Colombia aprueba presupuesto de gastos para 2027 por 634,9 billones de pesos
item.description: El Congreso de Colombia aprobó el martes el presupuesto de gastos para 2027 por 634,9 billones de pesos (201.168 millones de dólares), que contempla una reasignación de recursos entre diferentes sectores, un recorte en rubros relacionados con el acuerdo de paz y un incremento de los recursos destinados al pago del servicio de la deuda.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El Congreso de Colombia aprobó el martes el presupuesto de gastos para 2027 por 634,9 billones de pesos (201.168 millones de dólares), que contempla una reasignación de recursos entre diferentes sectores, un recorte en rubros relacionados con el acuerdo de paz y un incremento de los recursos destinados al pago del servicio de la deuda. La cifra supera los 555,8 billones de pesos del presupuesto vigente para 2026. El presupuesto del próximo año prevé un déficit fiscal de 9,4% del Producto Interno Bruto (PIB). El Senado aprobó la ley de presupuesto el lunes en la noche con 57 votos a favor y uno en contra, mientras que la Cámara de Representantes lo hizo el martes en la madrugada con 112 votos a favor y uno en contra. "Gracias a todos ustedes por habernos dado este voto de confianza, vamos a lograr sacar al país de esta situación económica tan compleja y para eso el presupuesto, sin lugar a dudas, es un primer paso muy importante", dijo el ministro de Hacienda, Miguel Gómez, después de la aprobación en el Senado. El Gobierno planea presentar al Congreso la denominada "Ley de Rescate" para recortar el gasto público el próximo año, con lo que el déficit fiscal se ajustaría al 7,2% del PIB, según el Ministerio de Hacienda. El presupuesto de gastos de 2027 asigna 141 billones de pesos (44.672 millones de dólares) para el pago de la deuda, 93 billones de pesos (29.464,7 millones de dólares) para educación, 84,6 billones de pesos (26.803 millones de dólares) para salud y 74,9 billones de pesos (23.730 millones de dólares) para defensa. RECORTES DEL GASTO La reasignación de recursos realizada por el Gobierno del presidente Abelardo De La Espriella provocó un recorte en el presupuesto de funcionamiento de la Jurisdicción Especial para la Paz (JEP) y la Unidad de Búsqueda de Personas dadas por Desaparecidas (UBPD), creadas en virtud del acuerdo de paz de 2016 firmado con la antigua guerrilla de las Fuerzas Armadas Revolucionarias de Colombia (FARC). El recorte a la JEP fue de alrededor de 181.000 millones de pesos, recursos que se trasladaron al Ministerio de Defensa, según el Ministerio de Hacienda. La reducción equivale al 23% del presupuesto del tribunal, un recorte mayor que el previsto. El tribunal advirtió que la decisión limitará las investigaciones y los juicios por violaciones de los derechos humanos, dificultará la prestación de asistencia jurídica y apoyo psicológico a las víctimas, así como el pago de sus gastos de viaje, y pondrá en riesgo los planes de seguridad para proteger a las víctimas y a los excombatientes. El presupuesto operativo de la UBPD se redujo en casi un 22%. La unidad, que busca al menos a 137.000 personas desaparecidas durante el conflicto armado, que continúa y ha dejado más de 450.000 muertos, ha advertido que un recorte de esa magnitud pondrá en peligro la toma de muestras de ADN de las familias y unas 10.000 exhumaciones previstas. La cuarta economía de América Latina enfrenta grandes desafíos para poner en orden sus cuentas fiscales, lo que elevará su endeudamiento público este año y el próximo, y la alejará cada vez más de la posibilidad de recuperar el grado de inversión que perdió en 2021. Además, el país sudamericano busca un acuerdo con el Fondo Monetario Internacional para conseguir financiamiento más barato y enfrentar el complicado panorama económico. (1 dólar = 3.156,32 pesos)

item.title: ニデック、永守氏や岸田氏ら9人の損賠責任認める 調査委報告書
item.description: ［東京 ２０日 ロイター］ - ニデックは２０日、会計不正などを受けた役員責任調査委員会の調査報告書（概要版）を公表し...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ニデック、永守氏や岸田氏ら9人の損賠責任認める　調査委報告書 10/20 18:05 配信

ニデックのロゴ。2026年9月9日、都内で撮影。REUTERS/Manami Yamada/File Photo

［東京　２０日　ロイター］ - ニデックは２０日、会計不正などを受けた役員責任調査委員会の調査報告書（概要版）を公表した。報告書は、創業者の永守重信氏について、グループ各社の会計不正の疑いについて取締役会・監査役会に報告して必要な調査を求めなかったことなどから任務を怠った監視義務違反が認められると指摘。同氏や岸田光哉前社長ら９人について、会社法などに基づく損害賠償責任を認定した。

ニデックは１６日に報告書を受領し、必要な非開示措置を施して２０日公表した。既に永守、岸田両氏らに対し、損害賠償請求など必要な法的措置を検討し、速やかに対応する方針を示している。９人には、過去に日本電産（現ニデック）社長を務め、現在は電子機器受託製造大手、台湾の鴻海（ホンハイ）精密工業で電気自動車（ＥＶ）事業の最高戦略責任者を務める関潤氏も含まれる。

報告書は「公正かつ透明性の高い資本市場を構築する屋台骨である企業会計（会計基準）及び会計監査制度が蔑ろにされてきた」と非難。その上で、モーター製造分野で世界をリードしてきたニデックが「現在（いま）を最後の機会と、不退転の覚悟で第三者委員会報告書の提言を確実に実行し、資本市場の信用を回復することを願う」と結んだ。

item.title: EssilorLuxottica's smart glasses boom runs into tougher regulatory scrutiny
item.description: Smart glasses that resemble ordinary eyewear are under increased scrutiny from European regulators and advocacy groups, leaving investors questioning whether sales can keep booming as Ray-Ban maker EssilorLuxottica reports third-quarter results.
item.dc:creator: Elisa Anzolin, Gianluca Lo Nostro, Elizabeth Howcroft
item.content:encoded: Smart glasses that resemble ordinary eyewear are under increased scrutiny from European regulators and advocacy groups, leaving investors questioning whether sales can keep booming as Ray-Ban maker EssilorLuxottica (ESLX.PA) reports third-quarter results. EssilorLuxottica launched its Ray-Ban Meta (META.O) smart glasses, capable of filming and recording, in 2023 and the market has grown rapidly. Global shipments of AI-enabled glasses jumped to 8.4 million units in 2025 from around 2.1 million in 2024, according to research group Omdia. EssilorLuxottica's Meta eyewear accounted for 81.3% of global shipments in the first half of this year. When it releases its third-quarter results on Tuesday, EssilorLuxottica is not expected to give precise data on the value of smart glasses sales, but may provide an indication. In its second-quarter trading update, it said smart glasses sales [USN:L1N43U0WL TEXT:"nearly doubled"] compared to the same period a year earlier. SOME GOVERNMENTS CONSIDER BANS The resemblance to ordinary eyewear has been a factor in the success of EssilorLuxottica's Meta smart glasses, and is in contrast to Google Glass (GOOGL.O) more than a decade ago, whose bulky, futuristic design limited mainstream consumer appeal. But the design's discretion is troubling to regulators. Last week, the European Data Protection Board, or EDPB, which brings together national privacy regulators, said the devices facilitated covert recording, including of bystanders' conversations. Louis Larere, portfolio manager at French asset manager BDL, echoed that concern. "The fact that smart glasses include a camera, allow users to livestream and instantly share content on social media could become a problem," he said. So far [USN:L6N45R0AS TEXT:"Norway"] has taken the toughest stance among governments, saying earlier this month it planned a temporary ban on the use of AI glasses in selected locations. [USN:L1N45908Z TEXT:"Australia"] said in September it was considering barring the use of camera-equipped smart glasses in government workplaces. In a preliminary, non-binding statement, the EDPB urged manufacturers to combine measures such as visible recording lights, sound alerts and notifications to nearby devices while recording. The authority also suggested limiting live streaming, automatically blurring bystanders' faces and using location-based technical restrictions in sensitive settings like hospitals or schools. PRIVACY CONCERNS MAY LIMIT ADOPTION Ross Gerber, CEO of California-based wealth management firm Gerber Kawasaki, which holds Meta shares, said privacy concerns and social stigma could limit wider adoption even though smart glasses still hold long-term potential. "People will make you feel uncomfortable if you wear them, and people feel uncomfortable wearing them because of this," he said, adding that his pair of Meta glasses was sitting unused in his garage. A Meta spokesperson said the glasses remain popular for music, calls and live translations. "They were built to be noticed which is why every pair with a camera has a bright light on the front that flashes when you take a photo or video you can share with others," they added. "It's important that rules protect people's rights while supporting innovation and consistency across technologies," an EssilorLuxottica spokesperson told Reuters, adding that the company is working to help consumers understand how to use the glasses responsibly and respectfully. Data regulators in Italy and Austria both told Reuters that they were investigating incidents involving smart glasses being used by pupils in schools, and [USN:L1N4590OL TEXT:"France's data watchdog"] previously said it had received a small number of complaints. "Authorities should think about banning these devices in public spaces in a more coordinated manner," Kleanthi Sardeli, a lawyer at European digital rights advocacy group NOYB, told Reuters. Growing privacy concerns could pose a challenge for EssilorLuxottica and Meta as they seek to position AI glasses, which can be used for making calls and listening to music, as a potential future alternative to smartphones. "(Privacy concerns) are a risk to this category. We already saw something similar more than a decade ago with Google Glasses," Cedric Rossi, luxury and consumer goods equity research analyst at Stifel, said. Rossi said Meta's unveiling in September of camera-free [USN:L1N45F121 TEXT:"audio glasses"] was a first step toward addressing regulatory and privacy concerns. However, he added that, without a camera, users cannot fully benefit from the AI capabilities the devices are designed to offer. Other companies, meanwhile, are still drawn to [USN:L4N42O1PB TEXT:"the category"] and Google, in partnership with Samsung (005930.KS) , plans to release its Gemini AI glasses before the end of this year. Apple (AAPL.O) is also expected to release its own smart glasses. BofA analysts in a report this month assessed the regulatory risk as limited and that an outright ban was unlikely even if additional restrictions emerge, particularly in Europe.

item.title: 中国・香港株式市場・大引け＝下落、追加景気対策への期待後退
item.description: [香港 ２０日 ロイター] - 中国・香港株式市場は下落して引けた。中国政府が主要政策金利を据え置き、国内総生産（ＧＤ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
中国・香港株式市場・大引け＝下落、追加景気対策への期待後退 10/20 17:59 配信

[香港 ２０日 ロイター] - 中国・香港株式市場は下落して引けた。中国政府が主要政策金利を据え置き、国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）指標は堅調だったことから、追加景気刺激策への期待が後退した。

中国本土のＣＳＩ３００指数は０．５％安で終了。上海総合指数は０．１％高となった。

ＣＳＩ銀行株指数は０．９％下落し、金融セクターは１．２％下げた。、金価格の下落が続いたことで金関連セクターは１．８％軟化した。

深セン証券取引所の新興企業向け市場「創業板（チャイネクスト）」総合指数は０．３％下落、上海証券取引所の新興ハイテク企業向け市場「科創板」５０指数は１％上昇した。

香港市場ではハンセン指数が１．３％下落、ハンセンテック指数は１．５％下げ、約２年ぶりの安値を付けた。

堅調なＧＤＰ（国内総生産）統計を受け、政策当局がさらなる金融緩和を急ぐ様子はないことを示す兆候として、中国は２０日、銀行貸出金利の指標となる最優遇貸出金利（ローンプライムレート、ＬＰＲ）を市場の予想通り１７カ月連続で据え置いた。

中国経済は前四半期に３年ぶりの低水準から持ち直し、４．５％成長と市場予想を上回った。堅調な輸出が低調な内需を補った。

メイバンクのアナリストはリポートで、全体として安定した成長が「新たな財政・金融刺激策を打ち出す緊急性を低下させている」と指摘。追加の刺激策がなければ、低調な国内投資と消費により成長はやや鈍化するとの見方を示した。

中小型株中心の北証５０成分指数は３．９％急伸して引けた。中国証券監督管理委員会（証監会）が北京証券取引所の発展を支援するため、連動する上場投資信託（ＥＴＦ）を立ち上げると表明したことが好感された。

item.title: 産学で医療画像処理システム開発、ラピダス先端半導体の活用念頭
item.description:
Kentaro Okasaka
[東京 ２０日 ロイター] - 国内の企業や大学、研究機関が参画する技術研究組合「最...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
産学で医療画像処理システム開発、ラピダス先端半導体の活用念頭 10/20 17:25 配信

ラピダスのロゴ。2026年8月21日、都内で撮影。REUTERS/Issei Kato

Kentaro Okasaka

[東京 ２０日 ロイター] - 国内の企業や大学、研究機関が参画する技術研究組合「最先端半導体技術センター（ＬＳＴＣ）」は２０日、回路線幅２ナノメートル（ナノは１０億分の１）の先端半導体を活用した医療用の画像処理システムの研究開発を、北海道大学や富士フイルム、ＧＥヘルスケア・ジャパン（東京都日野市）と共に開始すると発表した。

来年後半の２ナノ半導体の量産を目指すラピダス（東京都千代田区）が、米ＩＢＭから受託生産する製品の活用を念頭に置く。ＬＳＴＣ理事長を務めるラピダスの東哲郎会長は記者会見で「われわれが開発する半導体やＡＩ（人工知能）が人間の生活を豊かに、幸せにしていくことは最重要なことだ」とし、特に「医療分野における開発は非常に意義深い」と述べた。

研究開発は、独立行政法人の新エネルギー・産業技術総合開発機構（ＮＥＤＯ）の委託事業として採択された。ベルギーの半導体国際研究機関「ｉｍｅｃ（アイメック）」も加わる。医療分野でのＡＩ活用の障壁となっている消費電力と処理遅延の課題解決のため、医療機器内でリアルタイムに動作する高速・低消費電力の画像処理システム開発を目指す。

item.description: [２０日 ロイター] - ドイツ連邦統計庁が２０日発表した９月の生産者物価は、中東紛争によるエネルギー価格高で前年...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
独生産者物価、前年比＋6.7％で3年半ぶりの大幅上昇　エネ高響く 10/20 17:16 配信

2025年11月5日、ドイツ・デュイスブルクにある製鉄所。REUTERS/Leon Kuegeler/File Photo

[２０日 ロイター] - ドイツ連邦統計庁が２０日発表した９月の生産者物価は、中東紛争によるエネルギー価格高で前年比６．７％上昇し前月の４．６％から加速、２０２３年３月以来の大幅な伸びとなった。

ロイターがまとめたアナリスト予想は６．２％上昇だった。前月比では１．９％上昇した。

ベートマンＨＡＬのチーフエコノミスト、アレクサンダー・クリューガー氏は「生産の川上段階では引き続き強い価格上昇圧力がかかっている」と指摘。前年比の上昇率が１０％に近づく可能性が高いとし、「遅かれ早かれ、消費者物価も押し上げることになる」と語った。

上昇の主因はエネルギー価格で、前年比１４．９％上昇。中間財は６．４％上昇した。

item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
国内サイバー攻撃でＡＩ使用の有無、現時点で確たること言えない＝官房長官 10/20 16:53 配信

写真は木原稔官房長官。10月14日、都内で撮影。REUTERS/Issei Kato

[東京 ２０日 ロイター] - 木原稔官房長官は２０日午後の記者会見で、日本企業を標的としたサイバー攻撃の一部に中国系の人工知能（ＡＩ）エージェント「ＡＲＴＥＸ（アルテックス）」が使われたとの民間サイバーセキュリティ機関の調査結果について、承知しているとした上で、政府として調査分析を進めているところで「現時点で確たることを申し上げる段階にはない」と述べた。

政府は国家サイバー統括室が司令塔となり、関係省庁が集めた情報や被害企業のヒアリング、専門機関の調査を踏まえてＡＩが悪用された可能性を含めて各事案の詳細な分析を進めていると説明。「外国主体の関与の可能性も含めてあらゆる可能性を考慮しながら、攻撃主体や攻撃元の実態解明に努める」考えを示した。調査結果を公表するかどうかは、今後判断するとして明言を避けた。

item.title: 英賃金、6─8月は前年比＋3.7％に加速 雇用にも回復の兆し
item.description:
William Schomberg Suban Abdulla
[ロンドン ２０日 ロイター] - 英国立統計局（ＯＮ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
英賃金、6─8月は前年比＋3.7％に加速　雇用にも回復の兆し 10/20 16:37 配信

写真は英ストックポート、ハッターズヤード開発地区の建設作業員。7月14日撮影。REUTERS/Temilade Adelaja

William Schomberg　Suban Abdulla

[ロンドン ２０日 ロイター] - 英国立統計局（ＯＮＳ）が発表した労働市場統計によると、 賃金上昇ペースは再び小幅に加速し、雇用にもわずかな回復の兆しが見られた。来月の利上げの根拠を強める可能性がある。

６─８月の平均週給（ボーナスを除く）は前年同期比３．７％増加。今年に入ってから３．４％という最低水準を記録して以来、緩やかな上昇基調が続いている。

ロイターがエコノミストを対象に実施した調査では、３．６％増が予想されていた。５─７月の数値は３．６％増に上方修正された。

民間部門の賃金上昇率も２．９％から３．０％にややペースを速めた。２０２４年末以来の加速となった。

税務当局による給与所得者数の速報値は、９月に１万３０００人増加。８月の数値は、速報値の２万６０００人減から１０００人増に上方修正された。

求人サイト「インディード」のシニアエコノミスト、ジャック・ケネディ氏は「労働市場は一定の強靭性を示しており、経済全体が予想を上回るパフォーマンスを示している状況と一致している」と指摘。より力強く回復するかどうかは来週発表される予算案次第だと語った。

ＯＮＳが見直しを進めている調査に基づく６─８月の失業率は４．７％に低下し、２０２５年半ば以来の低水準となった。

データ公表後にポンドはドルに対して上昇した。

一方、７─９月の求人数は、６─８月の７０万４０００件から６９万１０００件に減少。２１年４月までの３カ月間以来初めて７０万件を下回り、新型コロナウイルスによるパンデミック期を除くと２０１４年以来の低水準となった。

会計士団体ＩＣＡＥＷのチーフエコノミスト、スレン・ティル氏は「求人数の継続的な減少は労働市場にとって警告であり、今年のＡＩ（人工知能）にけん引された経済成長の有害な副作用として、雇用需要の低迷が生じており、さらに人件費の高騰がそれを悪化させていることを示唆している」と述べた。

ＯＮＳによると、求人の減少は、人件費上昇の打撃を受けている小規模企業に集中した。

item.title: Gulf Keystone, ShaMaran agree $601 million oil merger
item.description: Gulf Keystone Petroleum said on Tuesday it would merge with Norway's ShaMaran Petroleum in a $601 million all-share 50-50 deal, creating one of the largest producers in Iraq's oil-rich Kurdistan region.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Gulf Keystone Petroleum (GKP.L) said on Tuesday it would merge with Norway's ShaMaran Petroleum (SNMS.OL) in a $601 million all-share 50-50 deal, creating one of the largest producers in Iraq's oil-rich Kurdistan region. Here are some details from the statement: ShaMaran shareholders to receive 0.07533958 Gulf Keystone share for each ShaMaran share held, with Gulf Keystone shareholders to receive a $50 million special dividend Merger combines operations across four Iraqi fields: Shaikan, Atrush, Sarsang and Hamrin Combined company expected to hold 323 million barrels of proved and probable reserves With pro-forma working interest production of 53,000 bpd, combined company ranks among the top 10 European listed independent oil producers Combined group has potential to reach 100,000 barrels of oil per day through development of Shaikan and Hamrin fields, a Gulf Keystone spokesperson said Dealmaking among Middle East-focused oil companies is supported by higher oil prices, with Genel Energy (GENL.L) competing with Norway's DNO (DNO.OL) to buy [USN:L6N45H0B2 TEXT:"Capricorn Energy"] (CNE.L)

item.title: France to deploy troops, admits to failures over weekend unrest
item.description: The turmoil shocked France inflaming tensions ahead of presidential elections next year.
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Pineau, Dominique Vidalon
item.content:encoded: France will reinforce police with troops and mount a huge security operation for more protests planned on Saturday, the government said on Tuesday, acknowledging failures in its response to [USN:L1N46401W TEXT:"last weekend's violence"]. "The deployment next Saturday will be massive," Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said, adding that the immediate priority was to restore order after rioting and looting swept Paris, Marseille, Lyon and other cities on October 17. In a sometimes rowdy debate, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said the military would be deployed alongside police, while the government pledged to overhaul tactics after widespread criticism that city centres had been left vulnerable. TARGETED CURFEWS HELP RESTORE CALM Framing the crisis as a choice "between violence and the Republic", Lecornu blamed the unrest on far-left groups, who in turn have accused the government of underestimating [USN:L1N4650EF TEXT:"public anger"] over high living costs and declining public services. The turmoil shocked France because of both its scale and the apparent inability of police to contain it, inflaming tensions ahead of presidential elections next year with candidates from the far right and hard left performing strongly in polls. Protests in other European countries, including [USN:L8N4650S6 TEXT:"Italy"] and [USN:L6N464038 TEXT:"Albania"], have added to concerns that anger over living standards risks spreading around the continent at a time when many nations, including France, are struggling with budget woes. A night of relative calm in France followed [USN:L6N4650BY TEXT:"targeted curfews"] imposed in several areas affected by the chaos, which the government said had helped reassert control. The localised curfews, some directed at children and teenagers under age 18, were extended to Tuesday night, police said. Lecornu acknowledged shortcomings in the state's response at the weekend, saying there had been intelligence failures, while police deployments had been too static and authorities had erred by not cancelling planned police leave. Nunez apologised for the mistakes. "I deeply regret what happened. I accept my share of responsibility," he said. SUSPECT ARRESTED FOR LIMOGES TOWN HALL DESTRUCTION Parliament is setting up a commission of inquiry to establish the causes of the unrest, while authorities have assigned 200 investigators to identify and track down those involved in the street violence. Police arrested on Tuesday a man suspected of starting a blaze that destroyed a historic town hall in the central city of Limoges during the rioting. Officials said he had been on a security watch list and belonged to an ultra-left group. Sylvain Maillard, a Renaissance deputy for Paris, told Reuters some apps had become "a walkie-talkie system for rioters and looters". Underscoring the broad impact of the crisis, French borrowing costs rose further on Tuesday as investors fretted about the prospect of more unrest, with the yield on benchmark 10-year government bonds touching its highest level in 24 years. Supermarket chain Carrefour said it had lost tens of millions of euros through [USN:L6N46612N TEXT:"theft and damage"], warning that it faced an "unprecedented situation" because of the disorder. France's main student union UNEF has called for further protests on Saturday, pledging to maintain pressure on Macron's government over what it says is a deteriorating and underfunded education system. "We carry on," it said on social media. Separately, groups identifying themselves as "Gilets Jaunes" (Yellow Vests) called for protest actions over rising fuel costs. The yellow vest movement, largely inactive in recent years, sprang up in 2018 during Macron's first term over plans to raise petrol taxes. Traffic blockades continued for months until the government made costly concessions it can ill afford now. ITALY FACES NEW FORM OF UNREST, MINISTER SAYS Northern Italian cities, including the financial capital Milan, were also hit by riots last weekend. Though not on the scale seen in France, the unrest nonetheless jolted Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's government, which was expected to introduce new security measures at a cabinet meeting on Tuesday. Defence Minister Guido Crosetto described the disturbances as a form of "hybrid warfare" conducted through social media platforms such as TikTok, YouTube and other online networks. "The events in Milan and elsewhere in Italy are fundamentally different from those seen in other eras," Crosetto wrote on X. "The West has yet to realise this or take any meaningful action in response." In Milan's central Corso Vittorio Emanuele II, sportswear retailer On and a Levi's store that were targeted during the unrest had reopened on Tuesday but remained boarded up. Luxury stores had restored merchandise to window displays after temporarily removing it for security reasons. In Albania, protesters were expected to take to the streets of Tirana for a seventh consecutive day against the government of Prime Minister Edi Rama.

item.title: China sends naval forces to monitor US warship near disputed shoal
item.description: China's military said on Tuesday it had sent forces to watch a US warship that "illegally" entered waters around a disputed shoal in the South China Sea, while further north in the waterway, Taiwan reported a standoff with a Chinese vessel.
item.dc:creator: Liz Lee, Ben Blanchard
item.content:encoded: China's military said on Tuesday it had sent forces to watch a US warship that "illegally" entered waters around a disputed shoal in the South China Sea, while further north in the waterway, Taiwan reported a standoff with a Chinese vessel. China views almost all of the South China Sea as its own territory, despite overlapping claims by Brunei, Malaysia, the Philippines, Taiwan and Vietnam, with recent tension most pronounced between Beijing and Manila. The Chinese military's Southern Theatre Command said the USS Charleston "illegally intruded" into waters adjacent to Sabina Shoal in the Spratly Islands without Chinese government approval in the early hours of Tuesday. "The US action infringes upon China's sovereign rights and interests, jeopardises maritime security, and is detrimental to regional peace and stability," it said in a statement. "The US side should immediately cease such activities." China's navy dispatched forces to track and monitor the ship, it added. A US Nay 7th Fleet spokesperson said the USS Charleston conducted routine operations in international waters consistent with international law. "All nations enjoy freedom of navigation and other lawful uses of the sea in this area," the spokesperson said in a statement. "The United States will continue to fly, sail, and operate wherever international law allows in support of regional peace, stability, and security." A Philippines' military spokesperson said the US ship "did not trespass into 'Chinese territory'," adding that no nation had the authority to require prior permission for "lawful transit through international waters." Last month, a China Coast Guard vessel [USN:L6N45A0A8 TEXT:"rammed"] a Philippine boat on a refuelling mission near the same shoal, according to the Philippine Coast Guard. China blamed the collision on the Philippine side. China and the Philippines, which has a mutual defence treaty with the US, both contest sovereignty over Sabina Shoal and the entire Spratly Islands archipelago. PRATAS STANDOFF In a separate incident on Tuesday at the top end of the South China Sea, Taiwan's Coast Guard said a Chinese Coast Guard ship had entered restricted waters near the Taiwan-controlled Pratas Islands. The Taiwan Coast Guard said its ship the "Taichung" was dispatched to warn away the Chinese boat, while both sides broadcast messages to each other. The Chinese ship broadcast that "the so-called Republic of China does not exist", referring to Taiwan's official name, while the Taiwanese ship broadcast back that "the Republic of China, Taiwan, is a sovereign and independent country", Taiwan's Coast Guard said, adding the standoff was continuing. China's Taiwan Affairs Office did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The office said last week that Taiwan must "bear the consequences" of its Coast Guard using a water cannon against a Chinese fishing boat near the [USN:L1N46003D TEXT:"Pratas"]. The Pratas Islands lie roughly between southern Taiwan and Hong Kong, but are only lightly defended and security is the responsibility of Taiwan's Coast Guard. China has also been stepping up coast guard activity around Taiwan, including off the island's east coast, causing concern in Western capitals. China views democratically governed Taiwan as its own territory. Speaking at a forum in Taipei on Tuesday, the chair of a review [USN:L1N46603C TEXT:"commission"] appointed by the US Congress said Chinese coast guard patrols to the east of Taiwan were "highly destabilising". Addressing the same event, Taiwan's National Security Council Secretary-General Joseph Wu said China had no legal claim to the waters off the island's east.

item.title: ‘It was crazy’: Australian barber hailed as hero after rushing to lawmaker’s rescue
item.description: Australian barber Ricky Jefferies said he ran to assist lawmaker Helen Haines, grabbing a knife from the alleged attacker's pocket and pulling him out of the car.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

‘It was crazy’: Australian barber hailed as hero after rushing to lawmaker’s rescue

Australian barber Ricky Jefferies said he ran to assist lawmaker Helen Haines, grabbing a knife from the alleged attacker's pocket and pulling him out of the car.

Barber Ricky Jefferies speaks to the media a day after tackling a man who attacked Australian politician Helen Haines in the northern regional city of Wangaratta on Oct 20, 2026. (Photo: AFP/William West)

FAST

SYDNEY: Australian barber Ricky Jefferies has been hailed as a hero for running out of his store to detain a man who authorities allege deliberately drove a car into lawmaker Helen Haines in the small town of Wangaratta, an incident that has shocked the country.    Jefferies had just finished haircuts for a young family on Monday (Oct 19) when he said he heard a "loud bang" outside his shop and realised the driver of a Toyota LandCruiser had struck Haines, leaving her badly injured. "It was crazy, I just ran out the front to see what was happening," he told reporters on Tuesday. He said he ran to assist the well-respected local MP, grabbing a knife from the alleged attacker's pocket and pulling him out of the car.

"He did have a knife. He didn't pull it out. I just wasn't comfortable with his movements, and so I basically just took it out of his pocket and threw it away," he said. Jefferies said he then held the man down until police arrived. "I just leant over him and once he was on the ground and he was no longer a threat, I just stood with him and I told him that he can't leave," he said.

Members of the police stand guard at the crime scene of a vehicle attack on Australian lawmaker Helen Haines in Wangaratta, Australia on Oct 19, 2026 in this screen grab obtained from a video. (Photo: Australian Broadcasting Corporation via Reuters)

Haines, 65, was airlifted to hospital where she underwent surgery overnight. She remains in a critical condition.  Early investigations suggested the driver, identified as a 43-year-old man, performed a U-turn before hitting Haines as she was loading or unloading things from the trunk of her car, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said . Counterterrorism authorities are among the multiple agencies involved in the investigation. While police have given no motive for the alleged attack, the involvement of counterterrorism investigators has raised alarm that it could have been an act of political violence, which is rare in Australia. Jefferies, whose shop is next door to Haines' electorate office around three hours' drive northeast of Melbourne, described the former midwife as a "genuine, kind person". Albanese praised Jefferies' intervention, calling him a hero. "At this dark and terrible time, an element of light is the fact that a Good Samaritan, someone rushed to Helen's defence in Wangaratta, put themselves potentially at risk by doing so. And that person is a hero today," Albanese said in an interview with the Nine network's "Today" show.  Jefferies downplayed the praise. "I don't think I'm a hero. I think that I just was a person who had an opportunity to intervene in a safe-ish sort of way," he said.

item.title: Stocks mostly rise as oil, US yields ease; French stocks fall
item.description: US stock indexes ended mostly higher as oil prices and Treasury yields eased on Tuesday, while French stocks fell as worries about unrest in the country remained.
item.dc:creator: Caroline Valetkevitch, Shashwat Chauhan
item.content:encoded: US stock indexes ended mostly higher as oil prices and Treasury yields eased on Tuesday, while French stocks fell as worries about unrest in the country remained. Helping the blue-chip Dow, 3M (MMM.N) shares shot up 5.8% after it said it was expanding its data-center partnership with Amazon (AMZN.O) . Shares of the industrial conglomerate were also boosted by the company raising its full-year profit forecast. After the closing bell, shares of [USN:L4N4661M0 TEXT:"SpaceX"] (SPCX.O) rose after the company said its third-quarter revenue more than doubled, beating estimates as AI and Starlink grew. The stock fell 0.1% in the regular session. At the same time, [USN:L6N465197 TEXT:"Netflix "] (NFLX.O) fell in after-hours trading as it gave a disappointing quarterly forecast. The stock was down 1.7% in the regular session. Quarterly results from AI heavyweight Meta (META.O) are scheduled for Wednesday. Investors are looking to corporate earnings for evidence that consumers and the broader economy remain resilient, but also that massive AI spending is paying off. "Investors really are waiting for the growth companies to report. Analysts have raised their estimates ... It's going to be by how much do they jump over that elevator bar," said Bruce Zaro, managing director at Granite Wealth Management in Plymouth, Massachusetts. Reflecting some of this nervousness was a 32% drop in South Korean AI [USN:L1N46600F TEXT:"infrastructure company"] Elice Group (0158S0.KQ) , when the stock fell below its initial public offering price in its market debut. Investors are also still assessing the risk that higher interest rates pose to AI stocks. Longer-dated US Treasury yields dropped, with the yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note down 1.5 basis points at 5.121% after falling as low as 5.073% on the day. Yields have risen recently amid worries about inflation. Expectations for a rate hike of at least 25 basis points from the Federal Reserve at its policy meeting next week stand at 17.2%, according to CME FedWatch, down from 22.1% a week ago and 57.6% a month earlier. "This is a market relieved that rates have come down, relieved that there's less volatility in oil prices, even though they remain elevated," said Jake Dollarhide, CEO of Longbow Asset Management in Tulsa, Oklahoma. "Earnings season can distract this market. Earnings season can give this market reason to go higher," he said. The Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) rose 529.85 points, or 1.02%, to 52,495.88, the S&P 500 (.SPX) rose 21.84 points, or 0.28%, to 7,712.57 and the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) fell 6.07 points, or 0.02%, to 26,424.82. MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe (.MIWD00000PUS) rose 0.42 points, or 0.04%, to 1,130.40. FRENCH STOCKS FALL, OIL EASES France's cities were [USN:L6N4660DJ TEXT:"calm overnight"] under curfews imposed after last weekend's unrest, while protest groups announced a new round of demonstrations next Saturday. French stocks (.FCHI) fell 0.38%, while the pan-European STOXX 600 (.STOXX) index was down 0.14%. European semiconductor companies including ASML (ASML.AS) and ASMI (ASMI.AS) also were lower. France's government [USN:L6N4660NP TEXT:"bond yields"] climbed further, with investors remaining cautious ahead of the plans for further protests. The unrest in France has underscored the difficulties the French government faces in reducing its large deficit. France's 10-year OAT yield earlier was up 3 basis points at 4.96%; it reached 4.9937%, its highest since July 2002, in early October. The yield gap between OATs and Bunds widened by 5.5 bps to 152.50 bps. The euro was up 0.22% at $1.1235, though traders remained cautious because of the unrest in France. Meanwhile, the [USN:L1N4660RH TEXT:"US dollar weakened"]. The dollar index , which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro, fell 0.25% to 101.71. Investors assessed the durability of strong capital inflows into US AI companies. Those inflows have supported the dollar. Higher interest rates, driven partly by growth and inflation expectations tied to the sector, have helped. Oil prices [USN:L1N46601X TEXT:"slipped"] after touching a five-month high. Investors [USN:L1N46601X TEXT:"assessed"] a meeting between the Iranian president and Pakistan's army chief, a key US-Iran mediator, against continued Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure that could disrupt supply. Brent crude futures fell 76 cents, or 0.69%, to settle at $108.79. Earlier in the session, the front-month contract reached $111.99, a five-month high. The November contract for US West Texas Intermediate crude , which expired on Tuesday, settled down $1.87, or 1.8%, at $101.79.

item.title: Trump warns Kansans that US will 'burn' like France if Democrats win
item.description: Trump used violent unrest in France as an argument against Democrats.
item.dc:creator: Bo Erickson, Steve Holland
item.content:encoded:
US President Donald Trump on Monday used [USN:L6N4650BY TEXT:"violent unrest in France"] as an argument against Democrats in his battle to defend a Kansas Senate seat long held by Republicans but in danger of falling to his political opponents. Trump's rally on behalf of Republican incumbent Roger Marshall was his latest foray into conservative states where Republican candidates are on defense due to voter frustrations over the Iran war and rising prices.

"I love you Kansas, but I'm here for a guy named Roger Marshall," Trump said. In a new addition to his stump speech, Trump pointed to widespread protests in France as a scenario that could erupt in the United States unless Republicans win. He provided no evidence. France in recent days has seen some of the worst unrest in years as huge protests over the cost of living and underfunded public services descended into riots and looting. Trump himself has struggled to make goods and services more affordable in the United States. In his speech, Trump turned to anti-immigrant and anti-Muslim rhetoric, the type that he used to fuel his three presidential campaigns. "We're not going to let that happen to this country," he said. "When you see burning steeples and raging fires in France, just remember that is what the radical Dumocrats want to do to America." Trump has been mocking Democrats by calling them Dumocrats. Rights advocates have [USN:L1N4620ZA TEXT:"repeatedly criticized"] Trump for his rhetoric over the years in which he has targeted and mocked immigrants and ethnic minority groups. Civil rights groups say such rhetoric normalizes discriminatory attitudes towards those communities. KANSAS COMPETITION Kansas, a conservative Midwestern state Trump won by 16 points in 2024, has not elected a Democrat to the US Senate in 94 years. First-term Senator Marshall is in a close fight with Democratic candidate Adam Hamilton, pastor of a Methodist megachurch, who is running against Trump’s tariff agenda and what he calls the president's “erratic leadership.” “He wants you to repent for being born White,” Trump said of Hamilton. Marshall, in remarks to the rally, led his campaign argument on cultural issues like stopping "radical Islam." He called Hamilton "too woke" for Kansas because he supports gay pride parades, which the crowd loudly booed. "We need someone who can sort heifers and steers," he said. In response, Hamilton's campaign spokesperson called Marshall's campaign "sinking." "Nothing said at the rally can distract from the fact Kansans are being crushed by rising gas and diesel prices, struggling to access affordable healthcare, and are tired of Washington corruption," the spokesperson, Tyson Brody, said. In a Monday video, Hamilton welcomed Trump to the state and said his supporters have “a place” in his campaign. Hamilton said he will work with Trump when it makes sense and stand up for Kansans when Washington policies hurt farmers and rural hospitals. The tightness of the race is emblematic of the challenges looming for Republicans in the November 3 midterm elections as they try to defy political headwinds and retain control of the Senate and the House of Representatives. Trump is deep into a 32-day campaign blitz, frequently going to friendly areas that he won handily in previous elections. One Republican familiar with Trump's midterm strategy said the president’s attention on rural parts of the country is in response to internal polling showing soft support from men 55 years and younger in rural areas nationwide, a voting bloc crucial to Trump’s 2024 presidential win. ECONOMIC CONCERNS The [USN:L6N46517O TEXT:"latest Reuters/Ipsos poll"], published on Monday, found that 31% of Americans approve of Trump's performance in office, a record low for the president. Democrats need a net gain of four seats in both the US House of Representatives and US Senate to overturn Republicans' narrow 218-214 and 53-47 majorities. In Park City, near Wichita, many rallygoers walked more than a mile across Interstate 135 to reach the rural arena, as a red-and-green truck stop sign flashed its latest prices above their heads: $3.98 for gas and $5.78 for diesel. That is up about 45% compared to average gas prices in the state last year, according to motoring club AAA. Economic concerns were palpable among Trump's most loyal supporters. “Being on disability, I don’t have much, but it seems like the prices are still going up and they need to come down. It feels like you’re having to search or hunt for food," said Monique Mullen, 59, a Republican voter from Hutchinson, Kansas, who takes care of her father. A small bloc of protesters gathered near the arena, including James Nightingale, a self-described independent from Halstead, Kansas. “I’m a farmer from Kansas and the Trump administration has decimated the farm economy in my area. Not only have his tariffs decimated our markets for grain sales, now he is bringing in imported beef from outside the country. What happened to ‘America First’?” he said. Kansans have proven a willingness to cross parties, as voters have elected a Democratic governor, Laura Kelly, for the last two terms. "I don't think it's ever easy to get elected here," said Gina Seman, a Trump voter from Towanda, Kansas, noting that Republican candidates in the past have taken their popularity for granted.

item.title: Gold edges lower as investors weigh Fed rate signals
item.description: Gold edged lower on Tuesday as investors weighed the likelihood of additional US interest rate hikes this year ahead of next week's Federal Reserve policy meeting.
item.dc:creator: Anushree Mukherjee
item.content:encoded: Gold edged lower on Tuesday as investors weighed the likelihood of additional US interest rate hikes this year ahead of next week's Federal Reserve policy meeting. Spot gold was down 0.3% at $4,125.90 per ounce by 02:05 p.m. EDT (1805 GMT). US gold futures for December delivery settled 0.4% lower at $4,142.60 per ounce. "Inflation and the Fed's interest rates are the big stories that gold's fighting at the moment. US Treasuries do appear more favorable than gold as a safety asset for the moment," said Bob Haberkorn, senior market strategist at StoneX. "$4,000 is a big level for (gold) to keep an eye on and see if it can hold. A lot of that, at the moment, is going to be dependent on what the Fed says," Haberkorn said. The Fed raised interest rates by a quarter point in September, its first hike this year. While recent comments from [USN:L6N462084 TEXT:"Fed"] officials signaling little [USN:L1N4600EO TEXT:"urgency"] for further policy tightening have tempered expectations of a rate hike at the central bank's October 27-28 policy meeting, traders see a 92% chance of a hike in December, according to CME's FedWatch Tool . FEDWATCH Gold is still down about 26% from its record high of $5,594.82 in January and roughly 22% from levels at the start of the Iran war , when concerns over energy inflation reinforced bets on interest rate hikes. Gold is traditionally seen as an inflation hedge, but it loses its appeal as a non-yielding asset in a high-interest-rate environment. Investors are also watching next week's US Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) data, the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge, for clues on whether inflation pressures remain persistent and how that could shape the rate outlook. In Japan, central bank Governor Kazuo Ueda [USN:L1N465004 TEXT:"said"] underlying inflation was "quite close" to the 2% target, signaling scope for further rate hikes. Among other metals, spot silver rose 1.4% to $57.86 per ounce, platinum gained 1% to $1,656.85 per ounce and palladium dropped 1.3% to $1,105.50 per ounce.

item.title: Trump open to idea of joint meeting with Xi, Putin next month
item.description: Nuclear talks between the US, China and Russia could happen as soon as next month after Donald Trump says he is open to a three-way summit.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

Trump open to idea of joint meeting with Xi, Putin next month

Nuclear talks between the US, China and Russia could happen as soon as next month after Donald Trump says he is open to a three-way summit.

Traditional Russian wooden dolls depicting China's President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin are displayed for sale at a souvenir shop in St Petersburg, Russia on Nov 21, 2024. (File photo: AP/Dmitri Lovetsky)

FAST

WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said on Monday (Oct 19) he is open to three-way arms-control talks with the leaders of China and Russia as soon as next month, raising the prospect of an unprecedented meeting and a major diplomatic gambit for the US president. "We would have it to talk about nuclear weapons and denuclearisation," Trump told reporters outside the White House. "If President Xi wants to have it, I'd have it. I'm sure we'd talk about other things like trade too." Trump has tried to thaw frosty relations with Beijing and Moscow as those non-Western powers grow closer. A three-way meeting would also raise alarm from Europe to Asia over private deals that weaken Washington's transatlantic and Indo-Pacific alliances. But a deal struck between the three countries could also lower global tensions. An end to Russia's war in Ukraine could resolve the biggest threat in decades to European security, and a deal on arms would bind the three nations with the biggest stockpiles of nuclear weapons.

In recent days, Trump has moved to warm ties with Russian President Vladimir Putin, announcing a diesel-fuel deal and signing an order on Friday waiving key sanctions on Moscow . Trump has also sought stable relations with Chinese President Xi Jinping, who in turn has nurtured close ties with Putin. So far, Trump has not delivered on a campaign promise to quickly end the war in Ukraine. The White House has been discussing for weeks a possible meeting between the leaders focused on denuclearisation on the sidelines of the Nov 18-19 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China, according to a person familiar with the matter. Putin later pitched using such a meeting to negotiate an end to the four-year-old Ukraine conflict in a manner that would favour Moscow, the Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the discussions. Putin's suggestion came during an Oct 9 phone call with Trump that yielded the deal on Russian diesel. Earlier on Monday, the Kremlin said that the potential meeting had come up in talks. The three leaders have met separately but never held formal talks together. The White House did not respond to a Reuters request for comment. The Russian and Chinese embassies in Washington also did not reply to requests for comment. Trump's diesel deal with Putin and the executive order waiving sanctions on Moscow have drawn criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy , who has warned they would embolden Putin and prolong the war. Speaking about the possible meeting on Monday, Trump said, "I would do it, not so much for Ukraine because Russia, frankly, has been fine on Ukraine." He added that "Zelenskiy is not helping matters much," and that "it's time for somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine." Moscow launched one of its broadest air assaults in months overnight, cutting power to more than half a million households and damaging energy infrastructure across Ukraine. Ten people were reported killed.

Related:

Commentary: Why do Trump and Xi keep meeting if the hard issues remain unresolved?

US and China discuss reciprocal visits to nuclear sites: Reports

TRUMP SEEKS NUCLEAR TALKS Last week, Trump told reporters he thought a denuclearisation deal with Russia and China was possible, but that it "doesn't have to be this year." It's not clear how advanced any talks between the countries are. Russia has the most stored nuclear warheads, followed by the United States and China, according to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute. The Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty expired earlier this year. The New START treaty, signed in 2010, allowed a single extension, which Putin and former US President Joe Biden agreed to for five years. Any new extension would require an executive decision to voluntarily extend the limits of the treaty. China's foreign ministry said last week that its "nuclear strength is by no means at the same level with that of the US and Russia" and that it would be "neither fair, reasonable nor realistic to ask China to join the so-called trilateral nuclear disarmament negotiations at this stage." Trump has already agreed to attend the APEC summit in Shenzhen next month, marking his second trip to China this year and his third visit with Xi over the same period. China, Russia and the United States are all members of APEC. On Monday, Trump downplayed the idea of another high-profile meeting in China, with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. "I get along with him very well, and I'm not sure that anybody's asking for a meeting," he said. Trump previously said he planned to meet with Kim this year. North Korea has publicly indicated that it is not open to talks aimed at convincing Pyongyang to give up its nuclear weapons.
